edge.what: Seven WAF rules per ruleset plus a response-side rule, live for every plan including Free
edge.caveat: 'This is a STOPGAP only' (CTO Dane Knecht); attackers mutated payloads; rules only cover traffic routed through Cloudflare; patch anyway

edge.what: Adaptive Security Engine rule 3000991 v1, 'PHP Remote Code Execution Attack Detected', both CVEs; existing command-injection rules also catching weaponised payloads
edge.caveat: 'The most effective defense continues to be the prompt application of vendor patches'

edge.what: A CVE-specific templated rule in the Next-Gen WAF that customers must enable; looks for 'bodies and parameters shaped in ways that differ from legitimate traffic'
edge.caveat: 'assume active mitigation will only serve as partial protection and may require blocking a substantial portion of legitimate traffic'

edge.what: Cloud WAF protected 'out of the box'; Elastic WAF and WAF Gateway after updates; inspects anomalous multipart payloads, repeated session fields, abnormal response headers, upload-progress activity
edge.caveat: Had the details under embargo; saw no matching traffic before disclosure

edge.what: No managed rule found; guidance to consider blocking multipart file uploads on PHP deployments that cannot be patched, after checking the application impact
edge.caveat: AWS's own PHP builds for managed distributions reportedly lagged the release (a reader's comment under the post, unverified)

edge.what: Three FortiGuard signatures (090502648, 090502651, 09052654) in database 0.00438, plus four custom-rule templates
edge.caveat: Signatures ship in alert-only mode by default; must be switched to block

signatures.text: Three independent repositories, all keying on request shape rather than payload bytes: the PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS field plus many array-form parts; duplicate or excessive multipart headers; a PHP worker spawning a shell. rjmendez retired its own earlier rules after finding the leaked proof-of-concept's mechanism did not match the fix. No rule from the Emerging Threats or Snort projects themselves was found.

A ModSecurity rule on the upload-progress field name (verified on 2.9.14, 'zero false positives by construction' once the feature is off), Sigma rules for the arm-phase fatal error ('in Unknown on line 0' means the bailout happened outside any script, in the multipart parse) and for FPM segfaults, Falco rules for a PHP worker exec or memfd, auditd for execve by the pool user. The guide notes ModSecurity's REQUEST_BODY is empty for multipart requests, so an earlier tripwire that matched it never fired.

signatures.what: The Hacker News, on what protects before the patch
signatures.text: Captured for the record; the newsroom's reading of it is on the exploitation page.

signals.signal: Multipart POSTs to endpoints that do not take uploads; bodies larger than memory_limit ending in 500 or 502; a burst of 500s from one IP followed by a slow 200
'Allowed memory size exhausted ... in Unknown on line 0' (an OOM outside any script, during request parsing); 'Failed to decode session object'
Clusters of Apache 'exit signal Segmentation fault (11)' or php-fpm segfaults in dmesg within minutes; nginx 'upstream prematurely closed connection' correlated with a prior fatal from the same IP
A mod_php or php-fpm worker spawning /bin/sh, curl, wget, or executing from memfd; with the known exploits no application code runs, so a shell from a worker is the exploit
New outbound connections from php-fpm or httpd workers to non-database endpoints

nginx's default log format records neither Content-Type nor bodies, so shape-based attempts are invisible there; no standard log carries the worker id the cross-request bug needs; a clean log proves little

exploitability.text: Attack complexity high (AC:H) and attack requirements present (AT:P): the attacker must defeat a built-in protection and needs conditions beyond the request.

'the existing PoCs require knowledge of the specific, running PHP binary and address space layout on the server for an attack to yield code execution on x86_64, so most deployments may be safe from RCE. Do not assume this holds true for you. If you operate a 32-bit PHP application, you should likely assume compromise.'

'Triggering the bug is much easier than turning it into code execution.' A later request must reach the same worker and place carefully shaped data. Five demonstrated techniques, three via upload progress; a memory disclosure of about 67 KB.
A lab reproduction of the leaked proof-of-concept's precondition produced a clean 200; 'VulnCheck independently reports that none of the public PoCs they reviewed have the correct mechanism'.
Had not built or reproduced a proof of concept and was not aware of public exploit code as of 20:30 UTC on 21 October.
'The PHP source tree calls the zend_bailout mechanism many places'; patching the demonstrated paths 'does not make the mechanism safe'. Expect more paths.
